center.locator: Midpoint between geometry:baksan-bno-building and the centroid of geometry:baksan-neutrino-village-boundary
center.note: Map centre only; not a claim about any structure.

levels.name: Surface
levels.note: The BNO administrative building and the Neutrino settlement.

depth_m.note: SAGE's own paper states 4700 m water-equivalent overburden and a horizontal distance of 3.5 km from the tunnel entrance, not a linear vertical depth; the 2100 m figure is the linear depth already recorded on site:baksan-sage-underground-lab, sourced only to Wikipedia (rank 12) this session. Left as an approximate range rather than reconciled further.
depth_m.quote: It is located 3.5 km from the entrance of a horizontal adit excavated into the side of Mount Andyrchi and has an overhead shielding of 4700 meters of water equivalent.

levels.name: Mount Andyrchi tunnels and underground halls
levels.note: No geometry feature is drawn at this level: no fetched source this session gives the tunnel's own path or bearing into the mountain (Overpass, which might show it as a mapped way, was unreachable throughout), so no sourced walk from the portal to SAGE's stated 3.5 km position was possible. See map.unlocated.

name: BNO — Baksan Neutrino Observatory
notes: This map is honestly thin: the surface administrative building and the Neutrino settlement are drawn from OpenStreetMap, but the tunnels themselves and the SAGE underground hall are not, because no fetched source this session gives the tunnel's path/bearing and OpenStreetMap does not appear to trace it (no way was found via Nominatim name search for 'Baksan tunnel' or Cyrillic equivalents, and a bounding-box tag search that Overpass would have allowed was not possible — Overpass was unreachable throughout this session, see the facility worklog).

SAGE's own 1999 paper (src:sage-1999-capture-rate) states the laboratory is '3.5 km from the entrance of a horizontal adit excavated into the side of Mount Andyrchi' with a 60x10x12 m chamber (src:geo-euro-ug-pandola-2011); this is recorded here and in the facility worklog as backlog for a future pass with Overpass access or a topographic source giving the tunnel's bearing.

Release geometry (underground): the Main adit entrance (OSM node) was added and the unlocated row now cites the official INR distances (550 m to BUST, 3.5 km to SAGE) and halls; the tunnel path and halls are still not drawn.

summary.plain: The Baksan Neutrino Observatory in the Russian Caucasus: the surface administrative building and the purpose-built village of Neutrino are drawn to scale; the SAGE gallium detector, 3.5 kilometres inside the mountain, has a sourced distance but no sourced path to draw it by.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:baksan-neutrino-observatory. Only surface features (OSM: the BNO administrative building, way 1504181774; the Neutrino settlement, way 206835293) are drawn. site:baksan-sage-underground-lab is left unlocated: SAGE's own 1999 paper gives its distance from the adit entrance (3.5 km) but not the tunnel's bearing, and Overpass, which could have supplied the tunnel's own OSM trace, was unreachable throughout this session.

unlocated.backlog: A published bearing or plan of the Main adit (INR technical drawing, the 'longitudinal section of the underground complex' of the INR page Fig. 1 with a plan view, or a topographic map of the underground complex); with the bearing, the BUST hall (550 m) and the SAGE hall (3.5 km) are one line-offset each from the entrance node.
unlocated.reason: Official INR pages give the layout along the tunnel but not in plan: two parallel horizontal adits about 4 km long into Mount Andyrchi; the Baksan Underground Scintillation Telescope hall 550 m from the start of the horizontal tunnel (base 16.7 m x 16.7 m, ~850 m w.e.); the gallium-germanium telescope (SAGE) laboratory 3.5 km from the tunnel entrance, with a 60 m x 10 m x 12 m hall at 4700 m w.e. No fetched source gives the adit's bearing or a coordinate for any hall, and OpenStreetMap maps only the Main adit entrance (drawn), not its path.
